title: Improving Support for Survivors of Domestic and Sexual Violence
what_it_is: Improving Support for Survivors of Domestic and Sexual Violence

sections.label: Support for violence survivors
sections.summary: Questions ask about social work strategy for therapy and support for family violence and sexual violence survivors' recovery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development what is the current strategy or practice in the social work and social services sector on the provision of therapy or support for families that have gone through family violence to aid in their psychological and emotional recovery from the trauma.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the current capability and capacity of the social services system in providing support to survivors of sexual violence in their mental, psychological and emotional recovery; and (b) whether the Ministry is currently working or plans to work with educational institutions to ensure a trauma-informed and survivor-centric approach to post-violence care and support for youths.

sections.label: Forensic psychologists at FVSCs
sections.summary: A taskforce recommendation will place a forensic-trained psychologist at each FVSC and PAVE to work with survivors and perpetrators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As recommended by the multi-stakeholder Taskforce on Family Violence, we will cater for a forensic-trained psychologist at each of the FVSCs and PAVE, to enable them to work more effectively with survivors and perpetrators.

sections.label: MSF works with TRANS SAFE
sections.summary: MSF is working with the third FVSC, TRANS SAFE, to enhance support for survivors of sexual harassment and violence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MSF is working with the third FVSC, TRANS SAFE, to enhance its capability and capacity to provide similar comprehensive support to survivors of sexual harassment and violence in the second half of the year.

sections.label: Family Violence Awareness Training
sections.summary: In 2021, MSF worked with 16 organisations to provide Family Violence Awareness Training to over 1,100 staff and volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2021, MSF worked with 16 organisations across the people, public and private sectors, including educational institutions, grassroots and religious organisations to provide Family Violence Awareness Training to over 1,100 staff and volunteers.

sections.label: Enhanced marriage preparation programme
sections.summary: MSF enhanced the marriage preparation programme to include adverse childhood experiences and their impact on relationships.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For instance, MSF has enhanced the marriage preparation programme to include topics such as adverse childhood experiences and its impact on relationships, with the aim of increasing couples’ awareness of family violence and building healthy relationship skills.

sections.label: Monitoring FVSC and PAVE capacity
sections.summary: MSF monitors FVSC and PAVE capacity, is prepared to increase it, and will cater for a forensic-trained psychologist at each FVSC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MSF regularly and closely monitors the capacity of our FVSCs as well as PAVE to ensure that they are adequately resourced to be able to provide effective support to clients who need their help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We monitor to ensure that they are able to manage their case load and when necessary, MSF is prepared to increase the capacity of the FVSCs as a whole, to be able to effectively help survivors and perpetrators of family violence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We had also recently announced that MSF will cater for a forensic-trained psychologist at each of the FVSCs to enable them to work more effectively with survivors and perpetrators.
